reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (confidence 0.45): SPY closed 11-06 at 735.29, about 1.05% above its 200-day (727.64), after -5.0% in 21 days, and the Nvidia governance shock plus December hike odds keep the backdrop fragile. Held-book review (L5), using marks derived from market_value/qty (intraday, so I also give a mark 4-5% lower): BTC/USD's stored invalidation (close more than 10% below the 83,685.83 fill, about 75,317) has tripped. The 11-06 close was 74,756, and BTC broke below $75K again this morning with ETF outflows. The exchange-failure clause is untripped (no exchange failed in the News input). The Skeptic's case against P1 is weak and I agree: the rule was written in advance, the position is about $13, and 'local bottom' is opinion. I approve selling in full (P1). L1 and L5 applied. P2 (VNQ): the Skeptic's serious objection holds up. This is the most rate-sensitive equity sleeve, bought into a week of inflation reports with December hike odds elevated, after a 21-day bounce (63d is -0.57%). A 0.315 beta understates its sensitivity to a rates shock, and the Market Analyst expects little appetite for adding equity risk. The Implicator found it small and diversifying (about 3.2% of equity at $20), and the Real Estate tilt is a Market Analyst favourite, so I do not reject it. But the owner wants the account mostly invested and cash is 11.4%, so I shrink it to a trial $12 rather than $20 (L4: that is about 1.9% of equity, justified by the Real Estate tilt and the low-beta diversification, not diversification alone). That is roughly the BTC proceeds, so the buy is close to a swap, not new risk, and cash stays near 11.6%, above the 10% buffer ($61.82) even if the BTC sale fills a little low. Orders should run sell first, then buy. The stance is risk-off and SPY sits 1% above the line, so I add no equity beta and no other new names today; INCY stays the first candidate if cash rises and the tape steadies. Other held names, distance to stop on the current mark and on a mark 4-5% lower: VOO/VTI invalidate on SPY below its 200-day (727.64, 1.05% away; a 4-5% lower SPY would breach it, and the code regime filter would then switch off buys and I would reassess at that close); IDXX about 676 vs 630 (about 7% away, about 2% on a mark 5% lower, about $2.4 of dollar risk to the stop at current weight, no earnings until 2027-02-01); MSM about 113.8 vs roughly 108 (about 5% away, so a 5% lower mark would reach the stop, position is only about $7.7); BND about 71.6 vs 70.0 (2.2%) and IEF about 92 vs 89.5 (2.6%), the nearest stops, both small and rate-exposed with inflation data this week; CARG about 33.7 vs 28.25 (16% away); DPZ about 336 vs 285; WMT, KR, MSCI, FAST, VRSN all 10%+ from their stops. No held name has earnings inside 5 trading days (WMT 11-19, KR 12-03). DPZ's guidance-cut item remains unconfirmed. Staples (WMT, DPZ, KR) are still about 26% by label and I am not adding (L3). I am only re-anchoring the VOO and VTI SPY line to the current 727.64 reading.
